transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-04-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex R. (Redwood AE), Priya N. (SE), Jordan L. (CSM); Marta G., Ethan P., Samuel B., Rina P. (HelioPay)
---
[00:00] Alex Romero: Great, hey everyone. Thanks for making time, this is the SLA and cost tradeoff exec brief, um, quick check-in to align on where HelioPay wants to land for payments inference.
[00:18] Marta Gomez: Thanks Alex. We've got folks from SRE and procurement on to make sure we can move from a pilot to a committed model without surprises.
[00:25] Samuel Brooks: Hi all, main thing for us is predictable latency under peak and clean PKI/KMS integration, regulatory audits are coming up.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Cool, we'll go high level then Priya (laughs) — sorry, bad segue — we'll go high level, then jump into numbers and the pilot plan.
[00:42] Ethan Park: Quick ask, can you not call it a "pilot" again without defining success, we burned cycles before — we need clear pass/fail.
[00:50] Jordan Li: Totally, we'll put clear SLOs in the plan, p95 and tail metrics and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:01] Alex Romero: Right, so where we landed after the last check-in: HelioPay's production usage pattern is spiky at 10:00–11:30 UTC and 18:00–19:00 UTC. Average tokens/day was 45M last month with 3x spikes. Is that still accurate?
[01:18] Ethan Park: Yes, with a note — promotional pushes push it higher, like 5x sometimes for 20–30 minutes.
[01:25] Priya Nair: That matters because batching and cache windows help cost but hurt tail latency on short spikes. Our system can do continuous batching, but for payments decisions you need sub-150ms p95 ideally.
[01:40] Marta Gomez: 150ms p95 is our internal bar for critical decisions, anything above that requires manual fallback which we want to avoid.
[01:47] Alex Romero: Understood. So tradeoff A: Hosted with smart routing and autoscale — lower ops, quick time-to-value, but slightly higher unit cost and less deterministic tail for very short big spikes. Tradeoff B: Dedicated capacity — predictable throughput, lower per-token, but commit required. Tradeoff C: Private (VPC/on-prem) — maximal isolation and control, more up-front work and infra ops.
[02:12] Samuel Brooks: If we pick dedicated, what's the typical provisioning time and the SLA?
[02:20] Priya Nair: Provisioning for dedicated pools is usually 5–10 business days once the contract is signed and capacity is reserved. We offer SLA-backed latency windows — depends on model sig and batch profile — but we can commit to 99.9% availability and a p95 latency SLO at an agreed sequence length.
[02:36] Ethan Park: Sequence length, right — our average prompt length is small but we have occasional long histories. Does that break the SLO?
[02:44] Priya Nair: We model the tail using your 7-day trace — that's why we asked for request logs. KV cache helps the common prefixes; long histories only hit the backend for the delta.
[02:56] Marta Gomez: About security, quick checklist: SOC2 report, SAML SSO, KMS integration (customer-managed), audit logs for access and inference inputs. Can Redwood confirm those?
[03:12] Alex Romero: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II, we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We'll send the redacted SOC2 and KMS hookup guide in the doc pack.
[03:24] Rina Patel: For procurement, we need the pilot terms and the cancellation windows and escrow for private variants.
[03:30] Jordan Li: We'll add that to the draft pilot agreement, also include a dedicated termination clause for non-performance measured by agreed SLOs.
[03:39] [04:00] (brief cross talk about calendar invites)
[04:18] Alex Romero: Priya, walk us through the benchmark plan you mentioned?
[04:22] Priya Nair: Sure. Plan is two phases: bench phase 1 is functional correctness and small load — validate output quality and prompt fidelity with your templates. Phase 2 is load: we replay a 7-day trace with amplified peaks to reproduce 5x bursts and measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll run it against three topologies: Hosted (standard), Dedicated (reserved), and Private (single-tenant) if you can provide infra for private.
[04:51] Ethan Park: For private, we need to know minimum HW footprint — number of GPUs and RAM. Do you recommend a quantized model for private?
[05:00] Priya Nair: We can recommend 4-bit or 8-bit quantization depending on quality vs cost. For most payment tasks, 8-bit runs fine and gives good latency. For private single-tenant with high throughput, 8xA100-equivalent is typical starting point — but we'll dimension precisely after we see your trace.
[05:20] Marta Gomez: Can you clarify model fallbacks? If a model degrades or there's capacity pressure, what's the graceful fallback path?
[05:28] Alex Romero: We use smart routing — if a model can't meet SLO we fall back to a cost-tiered compatible variant or route to another region or dedicated pool. You can opt-in for automatic fallback or manual.
[05:41] Samuel Brooks: Any data residency issues with routing across regions? We need EU-only for certain customers.
[05:48] Priya Nair: You can pin region and enforce routing policies to keep inference in-region. For private deployments we fully respect on-prem or VPC. For hosted, we offer region controls for EU/NA/APAC.
[06:00] [06:30] (brief pause, background noise)
[06:40] Ethan Park: About cost math — show us the delta between hosted and dedicated at our 45M tokens baseline and at 3x and 5x spikes. We need clear unit costs and amortized GPU cost assumptions.
[06:55] Alex Romero: We'll model three scenarios: baseline (45M tokens/month), 3x average, and 5x promotional spikes. For each we'll show per-token cost, projected monthly bill, and a recommended commitment level to hit >20% unit savings.
[07:15] Priya Nair: Also we'll include batching profiles — longer batching windows reduce cost but inflate p95 by Xms. We'll provide recommended batching config that keeps p95 <150ms for critical routes and uses aggressive batching for non-critical backfills.
[07:33] Marta Gomez: We have two class of calls: synchronous payment auth (must be sub-150ms) and async fraud scoring (ok to be 500–800ms). Can we isolate them?
[07:45] Priya Nair: Yes, route by policy to different pools. One pool can be dedicated for auth with tight SLOs, another served from hosted with higher throughput for async.
[07:55] Samuel Brooks: For canary and rollouts — we'd like automatic rollback if model quality drops. How do you support that?
[08:03] Alex Romero: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automated rollback based on eval metrics. You can wire up your quality checks and we can pause or rollback on regression.
[08:15] Rina Patel: For contract language, what about indemnity for incorrect inference leading to chargeback?
[08:22] Jordan Li: We'll loop in legal; usually liability is scoped with SLAs and a carve-out for customer prompt content. We'll surface precedent language in the pilot contract.
[08:34] [09:00] (keyboard clack)
[09:08] Priya Nair: One technical thing — KV cache settings: we suggest prefix caching for common templates. That reduces token compute for repeated prompts by about 30–50% in similar workloads but you need to ensure prompt hygiene.
[09:26] Ethan Park: We have dynamic templates with order info, does prefix caching still help?
[09:31] Priya Nair: Yes, if the template prefix stays identical, even with variable slots. For variable-length history we do delta encoding into the cache. We'll capture the exact heuristics in the benchmark plan.
[09:44] Marta Gomez: On observability, we need token-level billing tied to route, per-tenant latency histograms, and audit logs for inference inputs — is that shipped?
[09:55] Alex Romero: Yes — Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, route dashboards, and an audit log export. We'll show sample dashboards.
[10:05] Samuel Brooks: How long do you retain raw inference logs for debugging? GDPR and storage costs matter.
[10:12] Jordan Li: Default retention is 90 days for raw logs; you can configure longer for an add-on. We also provide redaction tools and data retention controls.
[10:23] Rina Patel: On KMS, does Redwood support enveloping with customer key?
[10:28] Priya Nair: Yes, customer KMS for key wrapping is supported; we can provide an HSM integration guide.
[10:35] Ethan Park: For the load test, will you simulate cold starts and KV warmups?
[10:40] Priya Nair: Yes, plan includes cold-start windows, warmup, and burst replay. We'll measure warmed p95 and cold p95 separately.
[10:48] Alex Romero: Ok let's talk timeline. Proposed: you give us trace by next Tuesday, we'll deliver a pricing packet and benchmark plan within 2 business days after that. Then schedule load test within the following week. Does that work?
[11:05] Marta Gomez: Yes, that schedule works. Procurement wants the pilot agreement before the load test so they can sign it.
[11:13] Rina Patel: Also need guarantee that pilot doesn't auto-convert to committed spend.
[11:18] Alex Romero: We will make that explicit — pilot is non-binding. Any conversion will be a separate contract.
[11:26] [11:40] (short side conversation about legal contacts)
[11:46] Samuel Brooks: Quick question — if we do private on-prem, who handles OS and driver patching?
[11:52] Priya Nair: For our packaged private deployment, we offer options: managed infra (Redwood handles driver and runtime patches) or customer-managed (you handle driver/OS). We'll document the operational responsibilities.
[12:06] Ethan Park: We need an estimate for managed vs unmanaged ops costs, please include that.
[12:12] Alex Romero: Will include ops staffing assumptions in the pricing packet.
[12:18] Priya Nair: One more note on model quantization — in our last similar engagement we found 8-bit reduced GPU needs by ~40% with negligible quality drop for short payment prompts. We'll include eval artifacts.
[12:32] Marta Gomez: Anything else on security?
[12:35] Rina Patel: Please send SOC2 and encryption docs.
[12:38] Alex Romero: We'll send SOC2 redacted, the KMS/HSM guide, and the SAML SSO flow diagram.
[12:44] [13:00] (murmurs, wrap-up begins)
[13:10] Jordan Li: Recap of next steps: Redwood sends pricing + pilot + SOC2 by 4/18–4/20 window; HelioPay provides logs by 4/19; schedule load test 4/27 tentative. Action items on the call will be shared in email.
[13:28] Marta Gomez: Good, appreciated. If pilot shows we can meet 150ms p95 on auth path and <20% unit cost delta versus hosted, we'll move to a dedicated commit discussion.
[13:39] Alex Romero: Great — that's the exact decision rule we'll use. Any final quick Qs?
[13:46] Samuel Brooks: Nothing else from me. Thanks.
[13:49] Rina Patel: Thanks everyone.
[13:52] Alex Romero: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
